lessons.title: Objects — The World Around You
can_do: Recognise twelve everyday objects by sound and picture
Match a spoken word to the thing it names
lessons.culture: Coffee and tea as the first act of hospitality: the cup is where the language starts.
lessons.video_scene: Objects shown one at a time while named — a cooking or home-tour clip where the speaker points at or holds the thing.

lessons.title: Greetings and Their Replies
can_do: Greet someone and answer their greeting
Say good morning, good evening and goodbye
Ask how someone is and say you are fine
lessons.culture: Every greeting has a fixed reply; the reply is the lesson. Handshakes, the right hand, and why 'peace be upon you' is answered word for word.

target_concepts.gloss: see you / God willing we meet

lessons.video_scene: Two people greeting each other at a door or on the street; street-interview intros are ideal.

lessons.title: Yes, No, Please and Thank You
can_do: Say yes, no, please and thank you and answer thanks
Apologise and get someone's attention politely
Use the everyday religious phrases everyone uses
lessons.culture: God-phrases are grammar, not piety: 'God willing', 'praise God' and 'what God wills' punctuate every conversation whatever the speaker's religiosity.
lessons.video_scene: Short exchanges at a shop counter or table: thanks and the reply, an apology, an 'okay'.

lessons.title: Me and You
can_do: Say who you are and where you are from
Ask someone's name
Point at yourself, the listener and a third person with the right pronoun

grammar.point: Subject pronouns: I, you (m/f), he, she
Nominal sentence — no verb 'to be' in the present

lessons.culture: Names and how people address each other: first names, 'father of…', the polite titles you will hear used on you.
lessons.video_scene: A self-introduction: vloggers introducing themselves, street interviews asking name and origin.

lessons.title: People and Family
can_do: Name the members of a family
Say 'my' and 'your' with family words
Ask about someone's family politely

grammar.point: Possessive suffixes -i and -ak/-ik (my, your)

lessons.culture: Family is the first thing people ask about. Which questions are normal, which are not, and why 'how is the family?' rarely wants a real answer.
lessons.video_scene: Family vlogs where members are introduced or called by name; a mother naming her children.

lessons.title: Numbers One to Ten
can_do: Count from one to ten
Ask how much something costs and understand the answer
Say a phone number digit by digit

grammar.point: How much? / how many?

lessons.culture: The local currency and its small change, and the fact that first prices are rarely final.
lessons.video_scene: A vendor quoting prices, a phone number being read out, children counting.

lessons.title: Food and Drink
can_do: Name common foods and drinks
Say what you want to eat or drink
Ask for something to be passed

grammar.point: 'I want' + noun — the first verb-like word

lessons.culture: The three meals, when they actually happen, and the dishes people are proud of. Eating with the right hand and from the shared plate.
lessons.video_scene: Cooking channels naming ingredients on screen; a family meal where dishes are named and passed.

lessons.title: This and That
can_do: Point at things with 'this' and 'that'
Ask 'what is this?'
Describe things as big, small, new, old, good, bad, hot, cold

grammar.point: Demonstratives: this / that (m/f)
Noun + adjective, adjective agrees with the noun

lessons.culture: Hot and cold are about drinks before weather: which drinks are served hot, which cold, and what to say about them.
lessons.video_scene: A speaker holding up or pointing at objects and describing them; market stalls, unboxings.

lessons.title: Where Is It?
can_do: Ask where something is
Say here, there, in, on and next to
Name the places you go every week

grammar.point: Where?
'There is / there isn't' + location phrases

lessons.culture: Asking strangers for directions is normal and expected; mosques as landmarks; where you can and cannot walk in.
lessons.video_scene: Someone giving or asking directions; a home or neighbourhood tour naming rooms and places.

lessons.title: Days and Time Words
can_do: Say today, tomorrow, yesterday and now
Name the parts of the day and the days that matter
Ask when something happens

grammar.point: When?
Time adverbs at the start or end of a sentence

lessons.culture: The day is shaped by the five prayers and the week by Friday; what 'the weekend' means locally and when shops actually open.
lessons.video_scene: A vlogger narrating their day with time words; morning-routine videos.

lessons.title: I Have, I Don't Have
can_do: Say what you have and don't have
Say there is and there isn't
Ask if someone has something

grammar.point: Negating 'have' and 'there is'
'With me / with you' and 'have' with suffixes

lessons.culture: 'I don't have a problem' and other no-problem phrases; how 'no' is softened and what 'God willing' means when it answers a request.
lessons.video_scene: Someone checking pockets or a bag, asking 'do you have…?' at a counter.

lessons.title: Survival Phrases
can_do: Say you don't understand and ask for slower repetition
Ask what a word means and how to say something
Say you speak a little

grammar.point: How do you say…? / What does … mean?
Polite imperatives: speak slowly, say it again

lessons.culture: How natives react to a learner — the delight, the switch to English, and the phrases that keep them in Arabic.
lessons.video_scene: A foreigner speaking Arabic on camera and natives helping; language-teacher channels.

lessons.title: My Daily Routine
can_do: Describe your ordinary day with eight core verbs
Conjugate the present tense for every person
Ask what someone does every day

grammar.point: Present tense — full paradigm of the habitual present

lessons.culture: The rhythm of a day: dawn prayer, the late lunch, the afternoon lull, the late evening when life starts.
lessons.video_scene: Day-in-the-life vlogs narrated in the present: 'I wake up, I drink coffee, I go to work'.

lessons.title: Asking Questions
can_do: Ask what, who, why, how, which, how many, when and where
Answer the small-talk questions everyone asks
Notice question word order

grammar.point: The full question-word set and where it sits in the sentence

lessons.culture: The small-talk interrogation: where from, married, children, what work — and the polite ways to answer or deflect.
lessons.video_scene: Street interviews (question then answer), quiz shows, kids' Q&A.

lessons.title: Saying No: Negation
can_do: Negate verbs, nouns and adjectives
Say never, nothing and nobody
Refuse politely

grammar.point: Negating verbs vs. negating nouns and adjectives

lessons.culture: Refusal is ritual: a first 'no' to food is expected, and how a real refusal is phrased so nobody loses face.
lessons.video_scene: Someone declining, arguing or saying 'no way' — comedy skits are full of it.

lessons.title: My House and Home
can_do: Name the rooms and main furniture
Use the full set of possessive suffixes
Say where things are in a room

grammar.point: Possessive suffixes — full paradigm — and the 'belonging to' word

lessons.culture: The guest room and the sitting room: who sits where, shoes at the door, and where guests are never taken.
lessons.video_scene: House tours; room-by-room narration; furniture named while shown.

lessons.title: Shopping at the Souq
can_do: Buy something and ask the price
Count from eleven to a hundred
Say expensive, cheap and ask for a discount

grammar.point: Numbers with counted nouns: 3–10 plural, 11+ singular
How much is this? / How much for…?

lessons.culture: The bargaining script from opening price to walking away, and when not to bargain at all.
lessons.video_scene: Market walk-throughs with prices; haggling; grocery hauls.

lessons.title: Ordering at a Café
can_do: Order food and drink
Ask for the bill
Say something is delicious, spicy or sweet

grammar.point: Imperative + object suffix: bring me, give us

lessons.culture: Café culture: who pays, the fight over the bill, tea and coffee orders with their sugar levels, and tipping.
lessons.video_scene: Café and restaurant scenes: ordering, the waiter, the bill; food-review channels.

lessons.title: Getting Around
can_do: Take a taxi or bus and say where you want to go
Give and follow simple directions
Say near, far, right, left, straight

grammar.point: Imperatives for directions: go, turn, stop

lessons.culture: Taxi etiquette: fixing the fare first, where to sit, and the local shared minibus.
lessons.video_scene: Taxi rides filmed from inside, directions being given, driving vlogs.

lessons.title: What I Did Yesterday
can_do: Say what you did yesterday and last week
Conjugate regular past-tense verbs
Tell a short sequence of past events

grammar.point: Past tense — full paradigm of regular verbs

lessons.culture: The weekend: which days it falls on, family visits, and the question 'what did you do on the weekend?'
lessons.video_scene: Vlog recaps in the past tense; 'what I did today' summaries.

lessons.title: Weather and Seasons
can_do: Talk about the weather
Name the seasons and say what they are like
Make weather small talk

grammar.point: Adjective sentences: 'the weather is hot', 'it is cold today'

lessons.culture: Heat as a way of life: the summer exodus, air conditioning, and the joy of rain.
lessons.video_scene: Weather chat at the start of vlogs; outdoor scenes commenting on heat or rain.

lessons.title: Work and Study
can_do: Say what you do and where
Name common jobs
Say you are busy or on holiday

grammar.point: 'I work as…' and the progressive 'I am (currently) doing'

lessons.culture: The working week, public-sector prestige, and how foreigners' jobs are asked about.
lessons.video_scene: Career or workplace vlogs; people describing their jobs in interviews.

lessons.title: Health and the Body
can_do: Name the main parts of the body
Say what hurts and that you are sick
Go to a pharmacy or doctor

grammar.point: 'I have' with symptoms: 'I have a headache'

lessons.culture: 'Your safety!' and its reply; visiting the sick as an obligation; home remedies people swear by.
lessons.video_scene: Pharmacy or clinic scenes; someone describing symptoms; home-remedy videos.

lessons.title: Plans and the Future
can_do: Say what you will do tomorrow and next week
Use the future marker
Make and accept an invitation

grammar.point: The future marker + present tense

lessons.culture: 'God willing' attached to every plan, and how to tell a real commitment from a polite one.
lessons.video_scene: Someone announcing plans: 'tomorrow we'll go…', travel-prep vlogs.

lessons.title: Describing People
can_do: Describe someone's looks and character
Compare two people or things
Say someone is taller or better

grammar.point: Comparatives and superlatives: bigger than, the best

lessons.culture: Compliments carry the evil eye: why 'what God wills' follows every nice thing said about a person.
lessons.video_scene: People describing friends or family; 'who is taller?' comparisons; comedy on character types.

lessons.title: Hospitality and Visiting
lessons.theme: Being a guest and a host
can_do: Welcome a guest and be welcomed
Offer and accept food and drink
Leave politely

grammar.point: Polite imperatives with suffixes: come in, sit down, have some

lessons.culture: The complete visit: the greeting at the door, coffee or tea first, the three refusals, standing up when someone enters, the leaving ritual.
lessons.video_scene: Home visits filmed: greeting at the door, coffee being poured, guests being urged to eat.

lessons.title: Telling a Story
can_do: Tell what happened with 'was' + verb
Sequence events with then, after that, while
Use the most common irregular past verbs

grammar.point: 'Was' + present/past for background; irregular (hollow, weak) past verbs

lessons.culture: Storytelling as social currency: the punchline, the exaggeration, and the listener's expected reactions.
lessons.video_scene: Someone recounting a story to camera or friends; storytime vlogs; comedy anecdotes.

lessons.title: Because, So and But
can_do: Give a reason and a consequence
Join sentences with but, although, in order to
Make an excuse politely

grammar.point: Clause connectors: because, so that, but, although, therefore

lessons.culture: Excuses and face: 'never mind', 'circumstances', and why the reason offered is often not the reason.
lessons.video_scene: Explanations and excuses in vlogs and skits: 'I was late because…'.

lessons.title: If and When
can_do: Say what you would do if
Use 'when' for future events
Express a wish

grammar.point: Conditionals: if (real / unreal) and when-clauses

lessons.culture: Hypothetical politeness: invitations phrased as conditions, and the wish formulas people use daily.
lessons.video_scene: Wishes and hypotheticals: 'if I had money…', 'when I travel…'.

lessons.title: Opinions and Feelings
can_do: Give your opinion and agree or disagree
Say how you feel
Say you like or hate something

grammar.point: 'I think that…' with the complementiser; opinion verbs

lessons.culture: Disagreeing without conflict: the softeners, 'in my opinion', and the topics best left alone.
lessons.video_scene: Opinion vlogs, reaction videos, debates on light topics.

lessons.title: The One Who…
can_do: Describe people and things with 'who / that' clauses
Say 'the one that I…'
Identify people by what they do

grammar.point: The relative marker for definite nouns; no marker after indefinite nouns

lessons.culture: Identifying people by role and relation — 'the one who works with your uncle' — in a world where everybody knows everybody.
lessons.video_scene: Descriptions of people and places: 'the guy who…', 'the place that…'.

lessons.title: Him, Her, Them: Object Pronouns
can_do: Attach object pronouns to verbs
Use prepositions with pronoun suffixes
Say 'tell him', 'give it to me', 'with them'

grammar.point: Object suffixes on verbs and prepositions — full paradigm

lessons.culture: Talking about people not in the room, and how gossip stays polite.
lessons.video_scene: Instructions and requests: 'give it to me', 'tell her', 'send it to us'.

lessons.title: Can, Must, Should
can_do: Say what you can and cannot do
Say what you must and should do
Ask for and give permission

grammar.point: Modal words + present tense: can, must, should, may

lessons.culture: Rules of the road, of the house and of religion as they surface in everyday speech; asking permission before photographing anyone.
lessons.video_scene: Rules explained on camera; 'you have to…', 'you can't…'; permission asked.

lessons.title: Phones and Messages
can_do: Make and answer a phone call
Send and reply to messages
Read common chat abbreviations

grammar.point: Negative imperatives: don't call, don't forget

lessons.culture: Voice notes over text, greetings that fill the first minute of every call, and the etiquette of the group chat.
lessons.video_scene: Phone calls in skits and vlogs; people reading and reacting to messages.

lessons.title: Celebrations and Condolences
can_do: Congratulate someone and answer congratulations
Offer condolences and reply
Talk about Ramadan, Eid and weddings

grammar.point: Set-phrase structures and their fixed replies

lessons.culture: The full occasions thread: Eid greetings and replies, wedding customs, birth, the condolence formula, and the gifts that go with each.
lessons.video_scene: Eid and wedding footage; Ramadan vlogs; congratulation exchanges.

lessons.title: Money, Rent and Bills
can_do: Rent a flat and discuss the contract
Pay bills and talk about salary
Count in hundreds and thousands

grammar.point: Large numbers, currency and prices in full sentences

lessons.culture: Cash culture, informal money transfer, the landlord relationship and what a lease really covers.
lessons.video_scene: Apartment tours with prices; salary and cost-of-living talk; bank or bill-paying scenes.

lessons.title: Social Media and Slang
can_do: Read informal posts and captions
Recognise the most common slang and laughter
Understand dialect spelling conventions and Arabizi

grammar.point: Participles used as tenses; dropped words in informal text

lessons.culture: Humour online: memes, laughter spelled out, emoji use, and the slang that marks a speaker's age.
lessons.video_scene: Reaction videos, meme explainers, influencers reading comments.

lessons.title: The Bridge: A Real Conversation
can_do: Hold a five-minute conversation on a familiar topic
Follow a two-minute authentic clip and get the gist
Self-assess and choose the next stage

grammar.point: Review: tenses in one conversation
Review: keeping a conversation going with questions

lessons.culture: Joining the conversation: the sitting-room and café topics that welcome an outsider, and how to hold the floor.
lessons.video_scene: A natural two-person conversation on a familiar topic, 2–3 minutes, clear audio.
